$schema-note: BardHero's recommended song list. This ships with the mod; the CHARTS DO
NOT. Each entry names a chart on Encore by hash, and tools/fetch_songs.py
downloads it onto the player's own machine - so nobody redistributes
someone else's audio or charting work, and the mod stays kilobytes.
Fields:
md5      - Encore's chart hash. It is the CDN key, not a checksum.
sha256   - of the downloaded .sng. Left out when pinning; the tool
records it on first fetch and verifies it forever after.
novideo  - true for charts with a video background, which fetches the
smaller _novideo package. BardHero renders no video.
note     - why this chart earned its place. Ignored by the tool, read
by whoever wonders later whether it can be swapped out.
artist/name - must match the chart's own metadata: the tool derives the
song folder from them to know what is already installed.
unlock_rank - OPTIONAL, 1-5. Written into the downloaded song.ini.
Only needed when a chart's ini omits diff_guitar, because
UnlockLogic reads an absent diff_guitar as rank 1 and would
hand the player its hardest songs first. Set it from what
another upload of the SAME song declares, not from taste.
Never overwrites a rank already present on disk.
To add a song:
python tools/fetch_songs.py search "artist title"
Search SCREENS each result on metadata the API returns: identical
difficulty tracks (compared by trackHash), six-fret GHL the loader
rejects, and a missing diff_guitar - which UnlockLogic reads as rank 1,
so the hardest chart in a set can arrive unlocked from the start. The
screen is validated against the pinned entry below, whose note counts
it reproduces exactly.
It only ever rules a chart OUT. PLAY a survivor before pinning it -
no metadata can tell you the audio is the right track, or that the
chart is any fun.
To install everything pinned here:
python tools/fetch_songs.py sync dist/SKSE/Plugins/BardHero/recommended-songs.json "<songs root>\guitar"

songs.name: You Shook Me All Night Long
songs.note: Play-tested. The 2026-07-25 Bridge audit made this the reference tracer: a real notes.mid with genuine Easy/Medium/Hard/Expert reductions (269/355/444/526 notes), seven Star Power phrases on every difficulty, and a dedicated guitar.opus stem. Three of the other four charts audited that day had identical or fake difficulty tracks, and a fifth was six-fret GHL the loader rejects outright - so this one is the standard the rest are measured against, not just a song.

songs.name: Freak on a Leash
songs.note: Play-tested. Harmonix's Rock Band conversion: 170/204/313/456 notes across four genuinely distinct difficulty tracks, with separate guitar, rhythm, keys, drum and vocal stems - so a miss drops the guitar out of a real mix rather than thinning the whole song. song.ini says diff_guitar = 1, so it lands at the bottom of the unlock ladder and is one of the first modern tracks a player can reach.

songs.name: Feel Good Inc.
songs.note: Play-tested. Harmonix's Rock Band conversion: 165/320/454/546 notes across four distinct difficulty tracks, full stem separation. The gentlest chart in the set at 165 Easy notes - the one to hand somebody who has never held a plastic guitar. diff_guitar = 2 puts it just above Freak on a Leash.

songs.name: Bat Country
songs.note: Play-tested. Harmonix's Rock Band conversion: 322/553/907/1381 notes across four distinct difficulty tracks, full stem separation. diff_guitar = 6 clamps to rank 5, so this is the top of the curated ladder - the reward for working up through the others rather than a starting point.

songs.name: Killing in the Name
songs.note: Screened, NOT play-tested - pinned 2026-07-27 on the owner's call that the classics carry their own recommendation. Harmonix's Rock Band conversion: 232/411/644/1357 notes across four distinct difficulty tracks, guitar plus five backing stems. diff_guitar = 3.

At 6:10 it is among the longest in the set, which the gold-scaling curve pays out for. diff_guitar = 5, so no unlock_rank override is needed.

songs.name: One
songs.note: Screened, NOT play-tested - pinned 2026-07-27 on the owner's call. The best-equipped chart in the set: 835/1323/1714/2146 notes across four distinct difficulty tracks, and the fullest stem layout of anything pinned here - guitar, bass, four drum stems, vocals and a crowd track. diff_guitar = 6 clamps to rank 5, so unlike the other Neversoft cuts it needs no unlock_rank override. A second Neversoft upload of One exists (md5 f199b1be..., 7:28) whose ini omits diff_guitar; this is the better one.

Verified 2026-07-26 to be the ONLY usable upload: of the four on Encore, two are Expert-only and one is six-fret GHL the loader rejects outright. Its ini omits diff_guitar, hence the override.

songs.name: Welcome To The Jungle
songs.note: Screened, NOT play-tested - pinned 2026-07-27 on the owner's call. 425/587/748/937 notes across four distinct difficulty tracks. This cut separates guitar, rhythm and backing. It trades away diff_guitar, hence the override.

songs.name: F.C.P.R.E.M.I.X.
songs.note: Screened, NOT play-tested - pinned 2026-07-27. 485/903/1198/1362 notes across four distinct difficulty tracks, guitar and rhythm separate from the backing. FINDING IT IS THE TRAP: searching the literal 'F.C.P.R.E.M.I.X.' works, but stripping the punctuation first does NOT - the tokens 'F C P R E M I X' match nothing, which is why an earlier pass wrongly concluded this song was absent from Encore. Four uploads exist; one is six-fret GHL and one is Expert-only. The alternative worth knowing is uSound/InternalDivide (305/599/985/1349, md5 4d02066b...), a different charting that declares diff_guitar = 6 and so needs no override. This one omits diff_guitar, hence unlock_rank mirroring that 6.
